messages:
rachel: noticed p95 jump on /v1/complete when switching chart aggregation from 1m to 5m. p50 constant. link: https://dash.redwood/ep/complete_tail

omo: Did anyone change histogram buckets or prom scrape config? histogram_quantile interpolation is sensitive to bucket edges.

viktor: I think we rolled a change to reduce histogram bucket cardinality in ingest (reduce buckets from 200->50) to save storage.

metrics-bot: ingest/config-change: histogram_buckets=50 from=200 at=2025-04-02T12:20:01Z user=viktor

rachel: That matches timeline. Our dashboard uses histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)) while SLO uses approx_percentile on rollups. The two methods can diverge when bucket width coarse.

omo: Can you export the raw numbers for the offending window? quick paste: overall p95(histogram)=260ms, p95(approx)=310ms, p50 both 120ms. The histogram has a big bucket boundary at 300ms causing interpolation to pull p95 down.

viktor: Oof. So stored rollups (approx_percentile) captured more accurate tail because they kept sub-ms samples, but histogram_quantile lost precision due to coarse buckets.

rachel: Implication: alerts based on histogram_quantile can miss regressions or show false regressions vs SLO query. We need consistent "query method" semantics exposed in Console and in alert rules.

omo: Proposal: (1) Add metadata pill that shows percentile method used per chart (histogram_quantile vs approx_percentile) and bucket_resolution for histograms. (2) For alerting, add a use-SLO-method flag so SLO and alert use same backend estimator. (3) Backfill histograms with finer buckets for last 24h for critical endpoints.

viktor: Also, add a warning when bucket_width > 20ms for any histogram used in percentile calculation. UI can show caution: bucket width too coarse for tail accuracy.

metrics-bot: job-schedule: run backfill finer-histograms for service=complete window=24h owner=viktor at=2025-04-02T12:45:00Z

rachel: Short term: annotate dashboards with ingest/config-change events and add the method pill + small tooltip explaining divergence reasons. Long term: migrate to t-digest sketches for percentiles and store bucket_resolution as metadata.

omo: I'll file ENGPLAT-1601 for method pill + alert flag, ENGPLAT-1602 for histogram backfill job, ENGPLAT-1603 for t-digest migration.

viktor: I'll run the backfill and a staging test comparing methods with synthetic skewed tails. We'll post numbers here.

rachel: thanks. this should reduce SRE noise where p95 disagrees between SLOs and dashboards. :thumbsup:
